newsitem.title: NORWAY: PGS wins $350 mln Conoco oil ship deal.
newsitem.headline: PGS wins $350 mln Conoco oil ship deal.

text.p: Norwegian offshore services and seismic company Petroleum Geo-Services ASA said on Wednesday it had been awarded a $350 million contract from U.S. oil company Conoco to build and operate a floating production ship.
The Ramform design floating production, storage and off-loading system (FPSO) will be used on Conoco's Banff field in the British sector of the North Sea.
"The company expects the contract to generate approximately $350 million of revenue over the first seven years of operations," PGS said in a statement.
The vessel's hull will be constructed in Korea by Hyundai Mipo Dockyard Ltd and the topsides will be fabricated and installed in Britain.
It will have an initial production capacity of 60,000 barrels per day and storage for 120,000 barrels.
The full system is expected to be delivered and ready for operation in June 1998.
PGS said it had subcontracted Atlantic Power to operate the unit.
